gen-fs-nippo-gf-lexend-peta: Nippo's small letters stand nearly as tall as its capitals, each stroke looking cut from wire. Lexend Peta follows in a plain sans with curves that never thin out, so paragraphs of it keep a wide-mouthed, friendly pace.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-lexend-tera: Technical and crisp, Nippo looks cut from wire. Lexend Tera sits beside it in a plain sans, drawn with a plotter pen's single line and spaced like stepping stones, so the page feels both precise and open.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-lexend-zetta: Approachable is the surprise here, since Nippo's wire-cut, nearly capital-sized small letters sit above Lexend Zetta's widely tracked, tall-bodied plain sans. Their strength is the contrast.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-liter: Modern and sharp, with Nippo's wire-cut letters up top. Liter takes over below as a sans with no stroke contrast at all and tall, wide-mouthed lowercase, so give it a modest size and let those proportions carry the text.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-mada: Nippo glows like neon tube, one line thickness throughout. Mada is the sans-serif below, low in contrast, with curves that refuse to close and a towering midzone, and that gap in character is what makes the pair work.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-martel-sans: Wire-cut and technical, Nippo draws like a rolling-ball pen on its way across the line. And Martel Sans, a sans with generous openings in every curve and a high mean line, gives the pair its strongest quality: a clear split between sharp heading and open text.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-matangi: Nippo's small letters stand proud, nearly capital height, with strokes that look cut from wire. Matangi's twine-like sans lines, open rounds and hefty lowercase make a long passage feel sturdy.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-maven-pro: Nippo leads with small letters nearly as tall as capitals and strokes that look cut from wire. Maven Pro then carries a long passage in a sans with a welcoming gap in the c, gentle line thickness and high-waisted lowercase.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-michroma: Technical describes Nippo well, its wire-cut strokes having no thick-and-thin contrast to slow the eye. But Michroma, a sans-serif with wide berth around each letter and tall lowercase with stubby ascender tips, is the one built for lingering.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-miriam-libre: Nippo brings wire-cut letters whose small forms rise almost to capital height. Miriam Libre answers in a sans with the weight of drawn wire, an open s and iron-tall lowercase, so heading and text feel cut from one workshop.
